pr_title: gh-102402: Fix floating point math issue by using `time.time_ns()` in `logging.LogRecord`
pr_body:
gh-102402: Fix floating point math issue by using `time.time_ns()` in `logging.LogRecord`.


+ Adjust `logging.LogRecord` to use `time.time_ns()` instead of `time.time()`.
+ Change method of calculating `LogRecord.msecs` to be robust against floating point / binary representation arithmetic errors
+ Added tests for the changes.


### Notes / Open Questions:

1.  `LogRecord.msecs` is a float so I kept it that way. Why is it a float even though it always has `.0`?
2.  In order to minimize impact, I kept `LogRecord.created` as a float in seconds. 
3.  I didn't see any type annotations in `logging.__init__` so I didn't add any for the new code. Would you like me to add some annotations?
4.  ~~I opted to use string manipulation to grab the `msecs`. I have an integer math-based approach, but it's, IMO, more verbose and harder to read/understand. LMK if you want me to switch back to that (there are still some minor fixes to apply to it).~~
    + I was able to come up with a math approach that is easy enough to understand.
6.  I wasn't sure of the best place to put the tests, so I just built off the other `msecs`-related bug.

Fixes #102402.

I was able to come up with a math approach that is pretty easy to understand. It's also faster.


### String manipulation:

```
$ python -m timeit -s "import time; ct=time.time_ns()" "float(str(ct)[-9:][:3])"
2000000 loops, best of 5: 162 nsec per loop
```

### Math:

```
$ python -m timeit -s "import time; ct=time.time_ns()" "ct_in_msecs = ct // 1_000_000; ct_in_secs = (ct_in_msecs // 1_000) * 1_000; msecs = (ct_in_msecs - ct_in_secs) + 0.0"
5000000 loops, best of 5: 74.3 nsec per loop
```

This version is a little faster:

```
$ python -m timeit -s "import time; ct=time.time_ns()" "msecs = (ct - ((ct // 1_000_000_000) * 1_000_000_000)) // 1_000_000 + 0.0"
5000000 loops, best of 5: 59.1 nsec per loop
```

issue_context.title: Logging's msecs doesn't handle "100ms" well.
issue_context.body:
# Bug report

`LogRecord.msecs` returns an incorrect value when timestamp (`self.ct`) value has exactly 100ms.


One liner check:

```python
assert int((1677793338.100_000_0 - int(1677793338.100_000_0)) * 1000) + 0.0 == 100.0
```

The issue is binary representation of "0.1" / floating point error:

```python
>>> # Definition of LogRecord.msecs:
>>> # https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/12011dd8bafa6867f2b4a8a9e8e54cb0fbf006e4/Lib/logging/__init__.py#L343
>>> # int((ct - int(ct)) * 1000) + 0.0
>>> ct = 1677793338.100_000_0
>>> ct
1677793338.1
>>> ct - int(ct)
0.09999990463256836
>>> _ * 1000
99.99990463256836
>>> int(_)
99
>>> _ + 0.0
99.0
```


# Your environment

- CPython versions tested on:
  - 3.10.9
  - 3.11.2
- Operating system and architecture:
  - Custom company OS based on Debian Testing
  - 64-bit


# Discussion

I think switching to [`time.time_ns`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/time.html#time.time_ns) when [setting the creation time](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/12011dd8bafa6867f2b4a8a9e8e54cb0fbf006e4/Lib/logging/__init__.py#L303) might be one solution.

<!-- gh-linked-prs -->
### Linked PRs
* gh-102412
* gh-117985
* gh-118062

comments: I agree with @dougthor42 about the proposed solution, since [time library itself suggests](https://docs.python.org/3/library/time.html#time.time:~:text=Use%20time_ns()%20to%20avoid%20the%20precision%20loss%20caused%20by%20the%20float%20type.) to "use time_ns() to avoid the precision loss caused by the float type".
I hope to find some time this weekend to implement a fix.

review_comments: Test also `created` and `relativeCreated` using `assertAlmostEqual()`. It is needed to ensure that they leave approximately the same, but `relativeCreated` should be now more accurate, and this can be detected if choose an appropriate `_startTime`.

Hmm... I'm not sure I understand. Can you elaborate?

This is what I understood:

```python
for ns, want in tests:
    ...
    self.assertEqual(record.msecs, want)
    self.assertAlmostEqual(record.created, record.relativeCreated)
```

However, that won't work because `relativeCreated` is set on module load, before we patch `time_ns()`, and they represent two vastly different things. I guess if we assume that `_startTime = 0`, then `self.assertAlmostEqual(record.created, record.relativeCreated)` would be `True`.

Were you thinking to also patch `logging._startTime` to a known value? Perhaps something like:

```python
    def test_issue_102402_relativeCreated(self):
        mok_startTime = 1_677_903_920_000_998_503
        delta_ns = 30_000_000
        ns = mok_startTime + delta_ns
        with patch.object(logging, "_startTime", mok_startTime):
            with patch("time.time_ns") as patched_ns:
                patched_ns.return_value = ns
                record = logging.makeLogRecord({'msg': 'test'})
        self.assertAlmostEqual(record.created, ns / 1e9)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(record.relativeCreated, 30)
```

Though I'm not sure how useful of a test the above example actually is... It seems like it's mostly testing _itself_.

Hence, I ask for more information 😁.

Yes, you need also to patch `_startTime`. The test is needed to check that there is no some silly error in computing `relativeCreated`, like using different scale. But we can also test that it is more precise now. Note that `assertAlmostEqual` allows you to specify `places` and `delta`, so you can test more precisely that by default.

Thinking about this more, it is better to not set `_startTime` explicitly, but patch `time.time_ns`, import fresh `logging` module, change the return value of the patched `time.time_ns`, and then make the record.

I think I understand now. PTAL at the new test. Ran the new test on `main` (well, cb944d0be8 as this PR is so old haha) and found that `relativeCreated` was only able to get about 3 places of precision. With this PR, that bumped to 7 places.
Do we also want to add `self.created_ns` as a public attribute?
There hasn't been a need for it thus far, and it's not necessary to fix the floating point representation issue. So I'd suggest not.
There should be a change in the module documentation as well.
I think it wouldn't hurt to check the `created` attribute here too.
Added. I went with `self.assertEqual(record.created, ns / 1e9)` instead of adjusting `tests` to be a 3-tuple of `(ns: int, want_msecs: float, want_created: float)`. LMK if you'd prefer the 3-tuple
It is all what I needed. Thank you.
